skill.name: image-outpainting
skill.description: Extend existing images beyond their canvas using RunComfy image edit models. The skill helps choose the right outpainting route, write preservation prompts, and run the RunComfy CLI.
skill.summary: Extend, uncrop, and reframe still images with RunComfy outpainting routes.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown backticks, catalog links, or documented credential storage, and I marked them false positive. I confirmed the command examples and package-manager guidance because the skill intentionally runs the RunComfy CLI and sends outpainting jobs to a third-party service. No prompt-injection attempt or covert data-exfiltration instruction was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution and package installation
remediation.suggestion: Keep allowed-tools restricted to Bash(runcomfy *), pin or verify the CLI version, and require user confirmation before installation or login.
Tell users that prompts and image references are sent to RunComfy, and require consent before processing sensitive or regulated images.
Never read or print the token file in agent workflows, and prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN from a secret manager in automation.

content.value_statement: Image canvas changes often require model selection, precise prompts, and preservation language. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through RunComfy outpainting routes and safe CLI use.
actual_capabilities: Selects RunComfy edit routes for aspect ratio changes, uncropping, reference matching, and brand-style continuation.
Provides RunComfy CLI examples for Nano Banana 2 Edit and related edit endpoints.
Shows prompt patterns that preserve the original subject while extending the canvas.
Explains when to use GPT Image 2 Edit, FLUX Kontext Pro, or ComfyUI workflows.
Documents RunComfy CLI exit codes, token storage, endpoint allowlists, and bash scope.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a valid RunComfy account or token.
Sends prompts and image references to RunComfy services for processing.
Does not perform mask-driven inpainting or video outpainting.
Complex seam repair may require a ComfyUI workflow outside the CLI.

use_cases.title: Social Format Conversion
use_cases.description: Turn square or portrait images into vertical, widescreen, or banner formats while preserving the main subject.

use_cases.title: Catalog Image Expansion
use_cases.description: Uncrop product shots and add matching background space for marketplace listings, ads, or hero images.

use_cases.title: Reference-Guided Restoration
use_cases.description: Extend cropped historical or editorial photos using reference images for period, lighting, and layout guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Widescreen Extension
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple aspect ratio change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Outpaint this image to 16:9. Extend the left and right sides with matching background, lighting, and perspective. Preserve the original subject exactly.

prompt_templates.title: Portrait Uncrop
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to reveal more of a cropped subject.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this portrait downward to show more upper body and arms. Match clothing, background, and lighting. Keep the face and current frame unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Reference-Matched Canvas
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that uses a style reference image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the original image and the reference image. Extend the canvas in the reference style, while preserving the original subject, pose, and identity.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Step Outpaint Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for large expansions that need multiple passes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a two-pass outpaint for this image. Extend no more than half the canvas each pass, inspect edge quality, and preserve the original content.

output_examples.input: A square product photo needs a wide marketplace banner.
output_examples.output: The result is a widescreen product image with matching surface texture, consistent shadows, and the original product unchanged.

output_examples.input: A head-and-shoulders portrait needs more vertical space.
output_examples.output: The result extends the lower frame with matching clothing and background while preserving the face and original crop area.

output_examples.input: A cropped landscape needs a cinematic 21:9 frame.
output_examples.output: The result adds plausible scenery on both sides with similar lighting, color, and camera distance.

best_practices: Use images supplied by the user and confirm rights for private or branded assets.
State the target aspect ratio and extension direction before preservation instructions.
Review output edges for seams before publishing or chaining another pass.
anti_patterns: Do not outpaint sensitive images without user approval for external processing.
Do not omit preservation instructions for the original visible area.
Do not use this skill for internal mask edits or video canvas changes.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps extend still images beyond their original canvas using RunComfy image edit models.

faq.question: Does it preserve the original subject?
faq.answer: The prompts emphasize preservation, but every generated result should be reviewed before use.

faq.question: Can it change aspect ratios?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides guidance for square, portrait, widescreen, vertical, and banner-style outputs.

faq.question: Does it work without RunComfy?
faq.answer: No. It depends on the RunComfy CLI and access to RunComfy model endpoints.

faq.question: Can it edit videos?
faq.answer: No. The skill covers still-image outpainting only and points users to a separate video workflow.

faq.question: Are private images processed locally?
faq.answer: No. Prompts and image references are sent to RunComfy services, so user consent is required.
